content.title: Phillies set Opening Day roster, filled with plenty of new faces
content.text: PHILADELPHIA -- Believe it or not, there are plenty of new faces on the Phillies’ 2026 Opening Day roster.In fact, there are 11 players who weren’t on the 2025 season-opening roster, including six new relievers, one starter, two outfielders and two bench bats.The Phils have seven days to trade Stubbs or place him on outright waivers. If he clears waivers, he can accept an outright assignment to Triple-A or elect free agency. If he elects free agency, however, he would forfeit the current contract that guarantees a relatively significant $575,000 Minor League salary.If the Phillies lose Stubbs, René Pinto would become the organization’s No. 3 catcher.He hopes to carry a strong second half in 2025 into his first All-Star season.The projected leadoff hitter again.He will be a free agent after the season, so he has plenty of motivation to have a big year.Crawford earned his spot this spring, even though he was a lock. Marsh and Kemp will platoon in left. The Phillies hope García can recapture the form that made him a Rangers legend in 2023.Crawford, Kemp and García weren’t on last year’s Opening Day roster.“Crawford has done very well for himself,” Dombrowski said. “He's played well in center field. Guys have been happy with him in that regard. So we feel that he's very comfortable out there. He has contributed from an offensive perspective. He's going to be ninth in the lineup most of the time. You have to suffer the ups and downs, which happens with young guys. But we like him a lot. He's meshed well. I think he brings a youthful enthusiasm, which is always great for a team.”The only question is where he hits in the lineup.Manager Rob Thomson said this spring that his ideal fourth bench guy is a true utility player, so it’s no surprise that Moore, who signed a Minor League deal in the offseason, made the team.“We like the versatility,” Dombrowski said. “We talked a great deal with the coaches and the staff members. Probably came down to him, Stubbs, [outfielder Bryan] De La Cruz. De La Cruz really had a good camp, we liked what he did. We just looked at the 26th spot right now, [it] was not going to get a lot of playing time, so we thought he'd be better off to go and keep playing. Be in a spot in case he's needed from injury perspective or performance perspective.“I try to work very closely with the manager on that last spot and how he likes to use guys. In his spot, he can use [Moore] in a bunch of different places. Help him if he wants to get guys off their feet. But there's no guaranteed playing time. I think he'll get enough, especially early in the season, getting people off their feet. But that was the reason behind it.”“He has thrown the ball very well this spring,” Dombrowski said. “He's done a good job for us. He just keeps building on what he has. His velocity has been very good. But more impressive has been his breaking stuff that he's been able to handle. He continues to build on that. So even though he's a young guy coming up that can throw upper 90s, he can also throw a sweeper, slider and changeup. He's earned it.”“He’s just not ready to go completely,” Dombrowski said. “Close, but that'll give him the chance to get ready properly.”Duran, Keller, Bowlan, Backhus, Pop and Mayza weren’t on last year’s Opening Day roster, meaning there’s a 75 percent turnover in the bullpen.“We just think Pop's been throwing great,” Dombrowski said. “He's always had good stuff. He’s got great sink. He's been up to 98 here. He has been throwing strikes on a more consistent basis than he has in the past. Tribute to him and the pitching people. Hopefully it keeps up. We'll see. But we think he earned the spot.”Rule 5 pick Zach McCambley has been returned to Miami.Senior Reporter Todd Zolecki has covered the Phillies since 2003, and for MLB.com since 2009.Skenes back to Cy Young form in win after tough Opening Day start7:33 PM UTCCINCINNATI -- Pirates ace Paul Skenes rebounded from the shortest outing of his career to post five strong innings Wednesday and earn his first win of the season, 8-3, against Cincinnati at Great American Ball Park.After allowing five runs on four hits, walking two and hitting a batter while retiring just two batters last Thursday, Skenes (1-1) allowed just one run on three hits, striking out five and walking two. He tossed 77 pitches (51 strikes) and lowered his season ERA from 67.50 to 9.53. Skenes left with a 4-1 lead thanks to an Oneil Cruz three-run homer off Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott (0-1) in the first.Mason Montgomery relieved Skenes to start the sixth, and allowed a pinch-hit two-run homer to Eugenio Suárez as the Reds cut the Pirates’ lead to one run. But Isaac Mattson, Justin Lawrence and Gregory Soto finished off the final 3 1/3 innings for Pittsburgh’s first series victory of the season.The Pirates have Thursday off before their home opener Friday afternoon against Baltimore.Bryan Reynolds blasted a two-run homer deep to the seats in right in a four-run ninth for his 140th as a Pirate, moving him into sole possession of ninth place all-time in Pirates history.Skenes didn’t give up a hit until Elly De La Cruz swatted a 90.1 mph changeup to right field for a single to open the bottom of the fourth. After Sal Stewart’s grounder moved De La Cruz to second, Nathaniel Lowe doubled him home, snapping Skenes’ scoreless streak against Cincinnati at 31 innings, dating to his first career start against the Reds on June 17, 2024.Coming into Wednesday’s game, the opponent figured to be the perfect elixir for the flame-throwing Pittsburgh ace after his shortest career outing six days earlier against the Mets in Queens.In five previous starts against the Reds, Skenes was 4-0 with a 0.31 ERA, covering 29 innings. He struck out 40 and walked just two batters. Skenes had not allowed a run against Cincinnati since the first inning of his first start against the Reds.Like his Opening Day start last Thursday, Skenes had an early lead to work with, this time thanks to Cruz belting his third homer of the series and season, and his second in as many at-bats.With two outs, Reynolds singled and Marcell Ozuna walked. Cruz then hopped all over a hanging curve from Abbott and unloaded it a Statcast-projected 407 feet to right for a 3-0 Pirates lead in the first.Skenes needed a batter to find his rhythm, walking leadoff man TJ Friedl on five pitches. But unlike his outing against the Mets, he quickly found a groove, striking out Matt McLain and De La Cruz before retiring the red-hot Stewart on a force out at second.
